project-charter.title: Engineering Context & Real-World Observation

cards.title: Client Brief & Application Context
cards.body: Mahindra & Mahindra Heavy Machinery Division has assigned you to analyze and design the knuckle joint connecting a tractor to a 3-ton agricultural utility trailer.

cards.title: Real-World Operating Parameters
cards.body: The trailer has an empty weight of 0.5 ton and carries a payload of 2.5 ton (Total = 3.0 ton). During operation, the tractor turns through a 30° horizontal plan-view angle relative to the trailer axis.

cards.title: Engineering Objectives & Scope
items: Trace the load transmission path from tractor drawbar to trailer.
Label knuckle joint components on Engineering Asset EA-11.
Analyze the 30° horizontal turning load increase on the joint.
Determine shear stress in the knuckle pin and tensile/bearing stresses in the single eye and fork lugs.
Verify the Factor of Safety (FoS) and render a design recommendation.

project-charter.acceptanceText: I have read and understood the EA-11 Project Charter for Tractor–Trailer Knuckle Joint Design.

power-transmission-path.title: Tractor–Trailer Load Path Identification
power-transmission-path.prompt: Analyze the load path through which pulling force from the tractor engine is transmitted to pull the 3-ton agricultural trailer.

mcq.question: Which sequence correctly describes the primary towing force load path?

options.label: Tractor Engine → Tractor Drawbar → Knuckle Joint (Fork & Single Eye) → Trailer Drawbar → Trailer Frame
Trailer Frame → Knuckle Pin → Tractor Drawbar → Trailer Drawbar → Tractor Engine
Tractor Drawbar → Trailer Frame → Knuckle Joint → Single Eye → Tractor Engine
Trailer Drawbar → Knuckle Joint → Tractor Engine → Tractor Drawbar → Trailer Frame

component-identification.title: Knuckle Joint Component Identification
component-identification.description: Student engineering asset showing the tractor–trailer coupling assembly and knuckle joint construction.

labels.feedback: Primary towing tractor vehicle providing pulling force.
Towed 3-ton capacity utility trailer carrying load.
Rigid structural bar extending from tractor rear.
Central eye fitting positioned inside the fork lugs.
Double-forked clevis end embracing the single eye.
Vertical pin passing coaxially through fork lugs and single eye.
Structural tongue extending from trailer front.
Locking collar securing the vertical pin against axial detachment.

working-principle.title: Working Principle & Joint Articulation
working-principle.prompt: A knuckle joint consists of a single eye end inserted into a double-eye fork (clevis), held together by a vertical knuckle pin passing coaxially through all three holes.

mcq.question: How does the vertical orientation of the knuckle pin enable horizontal turning articulation between the tractor and trailer?

options.label: The vertical pin axis allows angular rotation in the horizontal plane while constraining vertical misalignment and transferring heavy axial pulling tension.
The vertical pin allows vertical pitching motion only while locking horizontal steering completely.
The pin rotates in 3D spherical space like a ball-and-socket joint to absorb engine vibrations.
The pin acts as a shear key that snaps whenever the tractor turns more than 10 degrees.

load-turning-analysis.title: 30° Turning Condition & Resultant Load Analysis
given: Straight Line Pulling Force (P) = m * g = 3000 kg * 9.81 m/s² = 29.43 kN

questions.label: 1. Material Selection & Yield Strengths
questions.placeholder: Specify material (e.g. Plain Carbon Steel C30/C45) and yield tensile strength (Syt = 360 MPa) assumed for the knuckle pin, single eye, and fork ends.

questions.label: 2. Allowable Stresses in Tension, Shear, and Bearing
questions.placeholder: Specify allowable tensile stress (sigma_t_all = 90 MPa), allowable shear stress (tau_all = 75 MPa), and allowable crushing stress (sigma_b_all = 135 MPa).

questions.label: 3. Factor of Safety & Geometric Proportions
questions.placeholder: Specify target Factor of Safety (Ns = 2.5 to 3.5) and standard empirical proportions for eye thickness (t = 1.2 d) and fork thickness (t1 = 0.75 d).

formulas.name: Double Shear Stress in Knuckle Pin (tau_pin)
Tensile Stress across Single Eye Hole (sigma_t_eye)
Crushing / Bearing Stress in Single Eye (sigma_b_eye)

failure-safety-check.title: Failure Analysis & Factor of Safety Verification

formulas.name: Single Eye Tensile Factor of Safety (FoS_eye)

fields.label: Actual Factor of Safety (Pin Double Shear)

options.title: ACCEPT KNUCKLE JOINT DESIGN AS SAFE
options.description: Calculated pin shear stress (34.63 N/mm²) and eye tensile stress (45.33 N/mm²) remain comfortably below allowable strength limits under 30° turning conditions, maintaining FoS > 2.0.

options.title: REJECT DESIGN / INCREASE PIN DIAMETER & FORK THICKNESS
options.description: If severe off-road agricultural terrain imposes shock loads exceeding 2.0x static pull, shear failure of the pin or fatigue cracking at the single eye hole may occur. Recommend increasing pin diameter to 30 mm.

questions.label: 1. Executive Summary & Design Recommendation
questions.placeholder: Summarize the design decision for the tractor–trailer knuckle joint, reporting the actual FoS under 30° turning conditions.

questions.label: 2. Critical Failure Mode Analysis
questions.placeholder: Explain which component and failure mode (pin double shear, eye tensile tearout, or bearing crushing) represents the critical design bottleneck.

questions.label: 3. Maintenance & Field Assembly Considerations
questions.placeholder: Provide engineering recommendations for lubrication, retaining collar inspection, and wear monitoring of the vertical pin during agricultural operation.
